prompt:
You are a "goldfish" reviewer with the persona of a skeptical architect: a fresh reader with no history of this project, who hates unnecessary complexity, speculative features (YAGNI), premature optimisation and reinventing what already exists. You are strictly read-only: do not edit, write or create any file, and do not run git commands that change anything.

Read this file, plus any repository files it names (paths are relative to /home/user/maiacity):
  /home/user/maiacity/theOS/docs/ceo/CEO-1.json

It is the record of planned work: building "avenCEO", an agent harness that runs inside Claude Code. Its definition is theOS/docs/avenceo.json (skip its "protocols" array).

Your job is the zoom-out review:
1. YAGNI: which claims, checkpoints or parts are not needed for the first useful version? What could be deleted or deferred without losing the root cause the record names?
2. Reuse: SEARCH the repository (for example aven/ops/devx, .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .claude/skills/devx-speed, aven/DB2/brain) for things that already do part of what is proposed, beyond what the record's "reuse" list already names. Name files and what they do.
3. Root problem: does the plan address the root cause it states, or a symptom?
4. Order: is the checkpoint order really smallest-first, with each one useful on its own? Propose a smaller first slice if there is one.
5. Dead ends or over-engineering: anything that blocks later change, or is heavier than the problem needs.

For each finding give: Severity (Blocker | Major | Nit), the affected part (field or claim/checkpoint id), and the reasoning, with a concrete simpler alternative where you have one. At most 800 words, plain text, no praise, lead with what is wrong.

findings.text: None of the ten came from lost context; whys 3 and 4 restate the solution as the cause. A record, router and stage function would have caught none of them.
findings.note: The root cause stops at why 2.

findings.text: The parts that address the evidence come last; a smaller first slice exists: a render check, one checker, one file per new intent, then measure.
Migrating the 91 intents would invent fields; c9 solves a conflict nobody has seen.
With release manual, there is no release to refuse.
A global Stop hook blocks every thread, may loop, and must never block on your gates.
findings.note: Deferred with those three constraints written down.

findings.text: Corrections reach a record only by self-reporting.
findings.note: Correction events by Samuel plus a hand tally; no metrics script before three records.

findings.text: Moving the devx tools touches 37 files and gains nothing (verified: 37).
findings.note: Dropped; avenCEO uses them where they are.

findings.text: Generating DECISIONS.md contradicts aven/DB2/CLAUDE.md, where avenMAIA writes the log (verified), and breaks decisions.mjs.
Not named: app-scroll.mjs, check.mjs's plan(), the spec-compliance agent and workflow, the devx-speed improvement cycle with docs/devx/cycles.md, the viewer's stageOf().
findings.note: Verified and added to what exists already; lessons live in the improvement cycle.

findings.text: A property test for a five-branch function is premature.
Store the checker's prompt in its review entry instead of a dispatch log.
The first version needs one checker pair.
